transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah… I came in because I just don’t feel like myself anymore. Most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling right in my chest, like something’s been scooped out of me before the day even starts. And I keep thinking, you know, the old Ruben—the guy who could talk to anybody, make conversation, get through a day and actually enjoy parts of it—he just feels… gone. I don’t know how else to say it. It’s like I’m here, but I’m not really me.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It’s been… about eight months now, I’d say. I keep going back over it in my head, trying to figure out when exactly I started feeling this way, and it really lines up with when the new regional manager came in. He started coming down on me hard, watching everything I did, criticizing things that never used to be a problem, and then he started taking away accounts I’d handled for years. Accounts where I knew the people, knew the history, had built those relationships over a long time.

At first I told myself it was just stress, you know, just a rough patch at work, and that I’d shake it off once things settled. But it didn’t settle. It just kind of kept sinking in deeper. So… yeah, about eight months. That’s how long I’ve been feeling like this.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy before you started feeling this way?

Not really, no. That’s actually one of the things that bothers me the most, because I used to have things I looked forward to. I mean, I wasn’t some big exciting guy or anything, but I had my little routines, my things that made the week feel like it had some shape to it.

I used to bowl, for example. I had people I’d see there, and even if I wasn’t bowling well, I’d enjoy the joking around, the noise, just being out. And I used to like working in the garden too—getting my hands in the dirt, trimming things back, watching something grow. My wife and I would go to gallery shows sometimes, and I used to actually enjoy taking her, talking about the paintings afterward, maybe grabbing something to eat. We’d even go dancing once in a while, and I used to feel… I don’t know, alive doing that.

Now it all just feels like too much effort. I sit there and come up with excuses. I tell myself I’m tired, or it’s not a good night, or maybe next time. But the truth is, none of it feels worth doing. Even when I try, I’m kind of just there physically, waiting for it to be over.
Have you ever thought about hurting yourself or wished you weren't alive during these past eight months?

Yeah… I have. I don’t like saying that out loud, but yes.

It’s not like I’m sitting there every minute with some clear plan in my head, but I’ve had thoughts like… maybe it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. Or I start thinking my wife and the kids would be better off without me being like this, without having to watch me drag through every day and be this version of myself. And then I feel ashamed for even thinking that, because I know that would hurt them, but in the moment it can feel like I’m just a burden.

Those thoughts scare me. They scare me because I don’t feel like I can trust myself the way I used to. I used to be able to say, “No, that’s not me, I’d never think that way,” but now… I don’t know. The fact that the thoughts even show up makes me nervous.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels or the way you move, like feeling restless or slowed down?

I’m not really sure how to answer that clearly. I mean… I know I feel worn out a lot, but whether that’s my energy changing or just everything feeling harder, I don’t know.

As far as moving differently, I haven’t really noticed myself pacing around or anything like that. And I don’t know if I’m slowed down in a way other people would see. Sometimes I’ll sit for a long time before getting up to do something, but I can’t tell if that’s what you mean or if it’s more like physically moving slower.

So… I guess I’d say I’m not sure. I haven’t paid attention to it in that way.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past eight months?

I don’t really know, to be honest. I haven’t been keeping track of it in any careful way.

I mean, my clothes don’t feel dramatically different or anything that made me think, “Oh, I’ve lost a lot,” or “I’ve gained a lot.” But I also haven’t been stepping on the scale regularly. We have one in the bathroom, but I kind of avoid it unless I’m going to the doctor or something.

So… significant changes? I can’t say I’ve noticed anything major. If there’s been some change, it hasn’t jumped out at me.
Do you feel like you're moving slower than you used to, in your daily activities?

I honestly don’t know. I don’t think I’ve noticed it in a clear way, like I can’t say, “Yes, I’m walking slower,” or “people keep telling me I’m moving slow.” Nobody’s really said that to me, at least not that I can remember.

I do sometimes take longer to get started on things, like I’ll sit there looking at something I need to do before I actually get up and do it. But I’m not sure if that’s moving slower, exactly, or just… hesitating, or having trouble getting myself going. Once I’m up, I don’t know that I’m physically moving like an old man or anything.

So I guess my answer is I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid attention to whether my body is slower. It just feels like everything takes more effort, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing you’re asking.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're sitting still?

I’m not sure. I don’t think of myself as someone who’s constantly fidgeting, if that makes sense. Like, I’m not usually bouncing my leg so much that people comment on it, or getting up and walking around because I can’t sit still.

Sometimes when I’m sitting, I might shift around or rub my hands or pick at something, but I don’t know if that’s restlessness or just normal sitting there. I haven’t really paid attention to it in that specific way. I don’t have this clear sense of feeling driven to move, exactly.

So… I’d say I haven’t noticed anything major like that. If it’s happening, it’s not something I’ve been very aware of.
Do you often feel guilty or worthless about things you've done or haven't done?

Yeah… yes. I do. Probably more than I’d like to admit.

It’s this constant thing in my head where I keep telling myself I’m useless now. Like, I’ll think about all the years I spent working, taking care of clients, being the one people could count on, bringing money in, doing what I was supposed to do for my family… and then it’s like none of that counts anymore because right now I can’t even seem to handle this job the way I used to.

And I know, if someone else said that about themselves, I’d probably tell them that’s not fair, that one rough stretch doesn’t erase a whole life. But when it’s me, it feels different. It feels like I should be able to just push through it, and because I can’t, I must be failing somehow. So yes, I feel guilty, and I feel worthless a lot.
Have you experienced any strange or unusual thoughts, like hearing voices or seeing things that others can't?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve never heard voices talking to me or telling me things, not like that. And I don’t think I’ve seen things that other people couldn’t see.

Sometimes my thoughts feel strange in the sense that they get heavy or repetitive, like I can’t get away from them, but I don’t think that’s what you mean. It’s more like my own thoughts, not something coming from outside me. I don’t feel like someone is speaking to me or that I’m seeing people or shapes or anything.

So, no, as far as I can tell, nothing like hearing voices or seeing things.
Do you think you have been talking or responding more slowly than usual during our conversation today?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I mean, from inside my own head it’s hard to tell how I’m coming across.

I don’t think I’ve been intentionally slowing down or anything like that. Sometimes I pause because I’m trying to find the right words, or because I don’t want to answer too quickly and say it wrong. And I know I can kind of circle around an answer before I get to the point, so maybe it sounds slow in that way.

But I haven’t been sitting here thinking, “Oh, I’m talking much slower than normal.” If you’re noticing that, then maybe I am, but I can’t really judge it very well myself.
Have you been feeling an inner restlessness or agitation that makes you want to move around?

I’m not sure I’d describe it that way, no. I mean… I do feel uncomfortable in myself a lot, like I don’t know what to do with myself sometimes, but I don’t know that it’s a physical urge to get up and pace or keep moving.

During the day I might shift around or sit there feeling tense, but it’s hard for me to tell whether that’s actual restlessness or just me being unable to settle in my own head. I’m not bouncing off the walls or anything. I don’t think people would look at me and say, “He can’t sit still.”

So… I guess I haven’t really noticed that kind of inner agitation where I have to move around. At least not in a clear way.
Do you think other people have noticed you moving or responding more slowly than usual?

I don’t really know. No one has said that to me directly, like, “You’re moving slower,” or “You’re taking too long to answer.” At least not in those words.

I mean, I can imagine maybe people notice things I don’t notice. Sometimes when you’re the one doing it, it just feels normal from the inside, or you’re too caught up in trying to answer or get through the conversation to know how it looks. But I can’t say that anyone has pointed it out to me.

If anything, I’ve wondered whether I seem kind of… delayed or off, because I feel like I pause more and have to work harder to get my thoughts into words. But that’s me guessing. I haven’t had someone tell me they’ve noticed me moving slowly or responding slowly.
Have you lost or gained a significant amount of weight since you started feeling this way?

I’m not really sure, to be honest. I haven’t been tracking my weight closely or anything, so I can’t say, like, “I lost ten pounds” or “I gained fifteen.” I don’t weigh myself regularly.

My clothes don’t feel dramatically different, at least not that I’ve noticed in some obvious way. Maybe there’s been a little up or down, but nothing where I looked in the mirror and thought, “Wow, I’ve really changed,” or where someone commented on it.

So I guess the honest answer is I don’t know of any significant weight change. I just haven’t paid enough attention to be certain.
Do you think you've been having trouble concentrating or making decisions lately?

I’m not sure. I mean, I’ve wondered about that, because there are times I feel like my mind just sort of… doesn’t move as cleanly as it used to. But I don’t know if I’d call it trouble concentrating exactly, or if I’m just tired or distracted or overthinking things.

With decisions, it’s kind of the same. I can make decisions if I have to, but sometimes even small things feel like they take more effort than they should. Like I’ll sit there turning something over in my head longer than makes sense. But I don’t know if that’s something new enough or severe enough to say, “Yes, I have a problem making decisions.”

So… I guess I’d say maybe a little, but I’m not totally sure. I’ve noticed some difficulty keeping my thoughts straight at times, but I can’t give you a clear yes the way I could if it was really obvious.
Do you find yourself doing things like pacing back and forth or fidgeting when you're feeling anxious or upset?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think of myself as someone who paces back and forth a lot, at least not in a way I’ve really paid attention to. I mean, I might shift around or move my hands or adjust how I’m sitting, but I don’t know if that’s just normal restlessness or something more than that.

When I’m upset, I’m usually more aware of what’s going on in my head than what my body is doing, if that makes sense. So I could be fidgeting and not really register it. But I can’t honestly say, “Yes, I pace around,” or “Yes, I’m constantly fidgeting,” because I haven’t noticed a clear pattern like that.

I guess if anything, I’d say I haven’t really been aware of doing those things.
Do you find yourself doing repetitive movements, like hand wringing or tapping, when you're feeling anxious or upset?

I don’t really know. I mean, I understand what you’re asking—like wringing my hands or tapping my fingers over and over—but I can’t say I’ve noticed myself doing that in any clear way.

I might tap my foot once in a while or move my hands around, but I don’t know if that’s just normal, you know? I’m not usually watching myself closely when I’m anxious or upset. I’m more focused on what I’m thinking or feeling, so if my hands are doing something repetitive, I may not even register it.

I don’t think anyone’s pointed it out to me either, like, “You keep tapping” or “You’re wringing your hands.” So I guess my answer is… I haven’t noticed repetitive movements like that, at least not enough that I’d confidently say yes.
Do you think you have been speaking more slowly than usual during our conversation?

I’m not really sure, honestly. Sitting here, I don’t have a good sense of how fast I’m talking compared with how I normally do. Sometimes I feel like I’m pausing more because I’m trying to answer carefully, or because I’m searching for the right words, but I don’t know if that comes across as slow speech.

I mean, you’re hearing me from the outside, so you’d probably be able to tell better than I can. From my side, it just feels like I’m trying to think through the question and not give you some quick answer that isn’t accurate. I haven’t noticed people telling me I’m talking slower, or anything like that. So I’d say I don’t really know—I haven’t clearly noticed that in myself.
Do you think other people have noticed you speaking more slowly than usual?

I don’t really know. I can’t think of anyone saying that to me directly, like, “You’re talking slower than usual,” or “Why are you taking so long to get your words out?” Nobody’s put it that way, at least not that I remember.

I guess it’s possible someone might notice and not say anything. People don’t always point that kind of thing out, especially if they’re trying to be polite. And in my line of work, I’m used to talking a lot, so maybe if I were noticeably slower someone might pick up on it… but I haven’t had anyone tell me that.

So I’d say no, not that I know of. I haven’t really gotten feedback from other people that my speech is slower.
Do you often find yourself feeling like you need to be in constant motion, like pacing or fidgeting, when you're feeling anxious or upset?

I don’t know that I’d say “constant motion,” no. I mean, I understand what you mean—like someone pacing back and forth, can’t sit still, hands always moving, legs bouncing nonstop. I can’t really say I’ve noticed that about myself in a clear way.

When I’m anxious or upset, I’m usually more caught up in my head than paying attention to what my body is doing. I might shift in the chair, or maybe move my foot a little, but I don’t know if that’s anything more than what anyone would do. I don’t think I pace around a lot, at least not that I’m aware of. Nobody’s really told me, “You’re fidgeting all the time,” or “You can’t sit still,” anything like that.

So… I guess my answer is I’m not sure. I haven’t noticed a strong need to keep moving, like I can’t stop myself. If it’s happening, it’s not something I’m very aware of.
